purpose: Apply one causal macro-to-central-bank-reaction method to each G8 FX currency, with country-specific economic mechanisms and evidence requirements; not 8 independent scores.

method.always_start_with: Narrative of current level, direction, speed, breadth and persistence in real economy (firms, jobs, households) before model output.

stages.question: What is observed in firms, hiring/firing, wages, households, credit, inflation and growth? Separate levels, direction, acceleration, breadth and persistence.
Which mechanisms change the outlook over the next 1-2 quarters? Express an explicit cause-effect chain and say what is uncertain.

What does the central bank WANT to achieve; what CAN it do given its mandate, inflation, jobs and financial conditions? Define what makes hold, tighten, or ease more/less plausible, WITHOUT asserting a decision.
What was already priced in OIS/futures and 2Y BEFORE the macro release; what repriced afterwards? Separate front-end from 10Y growth, inflation expectations, term premium and supply.
Compare both legs of a pair, global risk, carry, positioning and price. Is the economic thesis valid but the trade unattractive?

causal_guardrails: No claim that a statistical correlation proves a causal transmission mechanism.
Do not infer what firms/consumers actually did from one proxy; phrase as a hypothesis until observed.
No numerical odds without calibrated evidence; base, upside and downside are qualitative.
A central bank decision today is not a commitment for future meetings.
Never infer 10Y movements solely from expected policy rates.
Do not label macro data 'point in time' unless released_at and vintage genuinely attest availability.
Do not fabricate OIS 3m/6m/12m readings; show quality-certified estimates separately from official rates.
Missing data must remain missing: no zero-fill, no invented consensus or releases.
Country narratives do not generate new directional FX signals until prospective tests warrant them.
No new dashboards, no redesign, no changes to D.json, approved FX Core or 28-pair ranking.
method.audience_output: Five to seven coherent sentences per currency: what we see; what changed; why it matters for firms/workers/households; possible bank reaction if data continues; markets priced vs surprise; counter-scenario and next decisive release.

firms: ISM manufacturing/services new orders and employment
corporate hiring plans and profit margins
inflation: core PCE services and housing trends
USD.reaction_question: Can Fed hold/tighten if demand stays firm and core inflation persists, or will labour weakness and slowing household demand rebalance risks?
market_check: Fed Funds and SOFR curves / OIS quality

EUR.mandate_focus: price stability; activity and labour matter primarily through future inflation and transmission
firms: bank lending standards, loans and funding costs
labor: negotiated wage tracker and compensation per employee
employment and labour shortages by country
EUR.reaction_question: Will domestic wage/services persistence justify holding policy tighter, or will weaker bank credit and domestic demand support easing?
market_check: €STR and ECB OIS/futures by tenor with quality labels
EUR sovereign 2Y and 10Y plus cross-country spreads

GBP.mandate_focus: 2% CPI price stability; subject to that, support government policy including growth and employment
firms: services PMI and business input costs
labor: private-sector pay growth and wage settlements
households: mortgage refinancing rates and debt servicing
real disposable income and consumer credit
GBP.reaction_question: How much can BoE ease if demand weakens but services inflation and wages remain sticky?
market_check: SONIA OIS tenor curves with dated provenance
sterling sensitivity to real rates and UK risk premium

JPY.mandate_focus: sustainable 2% price stability, including wage-price dynamics
inflation: underlying trend inflation vs import costs
services and domestically generated price pressure
JPY.reaction_question: Will sustained wage and domestic-demand improvements support further normalization despite external slowdown or import-price pressure?

CHF.mandate_focus: price stability; interest rate AND exchange rate influence monetary conditions
labor: skills shortages and recruiting plans by industry
inflation: Swiss CPI, domestic and imported inflation
CHF.reaction_question: Will CHF appreciation and weak inflation warrant easing or intervention, or could stronger domestic demand reduce that need?
market_check: EURCHF and global risk-off flow hypotheses
FX intervention possibility is NOT proof of actual intervention

CAD.mandate_focus: 2% inflation target with flexible attention to growth and labour outcomes
CAD.reaction_question: Can the BoC maintain restrictive rates if household refinancing and labour weaken, or does persistent underlying inflation require patience?
market_check: oil exposure relative to US and global risk

AUD.mandate_focus: dual price stability and full employment; CPI target 2-3%
labor: Wage Price Index and hiring intentions
households: real consumer spending and retail volumes
inflation: trimmed mean inflation and service prices
AUD.reaction_question: Does persistent domestic inflation outweigh slowing indebted households and labour, and how might China/global risk change the AUD response?
market_check: RBA cash-rate futures and OIS quality

NZD.mandate_focus: future annual CPI between 1-3% medium term, near 2%; maximum employment is not a coequal primary objective since 2023
firms: agricultural export income and China exposure
NZD.reaction_question: Does weakening household demand and non-tradables inflation permit RBNZ easing while financial stability and import-price risks remain?
market_check: RBNZ OCR pricing with honest proxy/estimation labels
NZD-AUD/USD rate differentials and China/risk beta

relative_pair_application.universe: 28 unique unordered pairs among eight currencies; direction assessed for both BASE and QUOTE, not 8 independent single-currency trade signals
questions: Which economy has the stronger change in activity and the more durable inflation-labour cycle?
Which bank's future path has more room to surprise relative to what each front-end curve ALREADY prices?
Could risk-off, funding, safe-haven flows or commodity exposure dominate the rate spread?
Do actual relative 2Y/OIS repricing and FX price confirm that causal story?
What evidence would overturn this contrast and why might the right thesis be a bad entry now?
relative_pair_application.interpretive_rule: A bullish economy narrative DOES NOT automatically imply an appreciation of its currency; the relative unpriced change matters.
